title: chant workspace records --since output
description: What `chant workspace records --kind <kind file> --since <rev|session id> --json` prints (#2673, #2650 C11): what changed in a kind's records between the commit --since names and the tree --at names, or the working tree without it. Records are matched by id; a record whose id could not be read is not compared. Between a review session's open and close commits, the changes are what the session did. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version. The change kinds and the error codes are closed lists. Contract version 1 is written by chant 0.81.0 and newer, and this document was added to it by #2673; a chant without --since on records refuses the flag. Every code is in the one closed list of `reason-codes.ts`.

set.description: Added in contract 1 by #2680. What records --since prints without --kind when the workspace declaration names record kinds: one result or failure per declared kind, in the declaration's order (the workspace's own kinds, then each member's in member order). Exit code 1 when any kind's read failed; the others are still compared and listed.

declared.description: The declaration's entry for the kind, as in the records set.

result.description: Both revisions were read. Exit code 0, whatever changed.

name.description: The kind's name, such as "decision" or "session".

schema.description: The `$id` of the kind's record schema.

file.description: The kind file, relative to the repository root, with / separators. It is read from the working tree for both revisions.

at.description: The full commit id --at names, or null for the working tree.

changes.description: In the order new, removed, state, verdict, supersession, pin, and by id within each.

summary.description: How many changes of each kind.

session.description: Added in contract 1 by #2693, with --since <session id> only: the session named, and where since and at came from. since is the commit the session opened at: its opening revision field (the kind's session.openedRev), or, for a session without one, the latest commit that added its file (history). at is the commit that carries the close: the first commit after its closing revision field (session.closedRev, HEAD when records close wrote the close) that changed the session file (close-commit), or, for a session without that field, the last commit that changed its file (history); --at overrides it (at). An open session, or one whose close is not committed yet, is compared with the working tree (working-tree), and an open one carries since-session-open.

path.description: The session file, from the repository root, with / separators.

new.description: A record with an id no record had at --since. A directory that did not exist at --since held no records, so every record in it is new.

path.description: From the repository root, with / separators.

removed.description: A record whose id no record has any more.

state.description: A state transition, such as decided to ratified, or a session open to closed.

verdict.description: A verdict the record did not have at --since, including every verdict on a new record. On a session it is an entry of the session's verdict list, with the record it judged in record; on any other record, an entry of its reviews list, with the session it was given in when it names one. Two entries are the same verdict when they name the same principal, verdict, date, session and record, so a dissent that later gains addressed_by is not a new one.

principal.description: Who gave it, as written: a review's reviewer, or a session verdict's principal.

verdict.description: agree, dissent or abstain, as written.

index.description: Its position in the list, from 0.

record.description: On a session's verdict, the record it judged.

session.description: On a review entry, the session it names.

supersession.description: A supersession that took effect since --since, derived by the same rule as records' supersededBy, so a pending link that is now approved counts.

pin.description: A pinned file whose pinned sha256 changed on a record that exists at both revisions: from is null for a pin added, and to is null for a pin removed.

path.description: From the workspace root, as the pin writes it.

failure.description: A revision or the kind could not be read. Exit code 1.
